description.value: Secondary fMRI analyses examined whether lifetime DSM-IV-TR withdrawal history modulated drug-versus-food cue reactivity in cocaine-dependent participants, including effects of drug-use history and psychopathic traits.

spans.text: The current study offers insight into these conflicting positions by using secondary analyses to assess how a history of DSM-assessed withdrawal influences the magnitude of bias in neural reactivity to drug- and/or food-related reward cues.

design.value: A mixed-model flexible-factorial fMRI study compared WD, N-WD, and ND groups across DRUG and FOOD video conditions, with exploratory hierarchical regression analyses among dependent participants.

spans.text: A mixed-model flexible-factorial analysis included Group (WD, N-WD, ND), VideoType (DRUG, FOOD) and the Group*VideoType interaction in the model.

### Cue-elicited craving task

task_description.value: Participants viewed cocaine-related and food-related videos during two identical fMRI runs.

spans.text: Participants were presented with two identical runs during which they viewed 29 videos (duration: ∼10,000–14,000 ms): 15 videos depicted individuals preparing or using cocaine, and 14 videos depicted individuals preparing or eating food.
Videos were separated by an inter-trial jitter of either 2000, 3500, or 5000 ms to aid deconvolution from the standard hemodynamic response function.
